question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
Under the National Building Research Institute Act, No. 20 of 2025 (certified 2025-10-07) — not a bill, it has been enacted — an officer or employee who wishes to opt out "may do so within six months from the date on which he was offered employment in the Institute" [Act 20/2025 §33(2)(b)].

- The option applies to officers/employees of the former National Building Research Organisation still in service and below retirement age [Act 20/2025 §33(2)(a)].
- If the option is exercised, compensation is payable "under a voluntary retirement scheme" approved by the Minister and the Minister of Finance [Act 20/2025 §33(2)(c)].

Caveats: The text does not say how notice of the offer is given; no other passage sets a decision period.

question: Under the proposed Inland Revenue amendment, from which assessment date are deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act excluded from subsection (2)?
answer:
The exclusion applies to amounts deducted under section 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act "for any year of assessment prior to April 1, 2018" [Act 11/2026 §34].

- This is now law, not a bill: Inland Revenue (Amendment) Act, No. 11 of 2026 (certified 2026-06-03), amending the Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017 [Act 11/2026 §34].
- The new subsection (2A) inserted after section 202(2) is expressly "for the avoidance of doubt", and covers that pre-1 April 2018 period "notwithstanding that any un-deducted balance of such deduction under the repealed Act remains as at April 1, 2018" [Act 11/2026 §34].

Caveats: The evidence gives only the amending text, not the full current text of section 202 of the principal enactment.

question: Under the proposed Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority law, how long does a licence issued or renewed remain in effect?
answer:
Under the certified Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority Act, No. 9 of 2026, a licence issued under section 23 or renewed under section 24 is "valid for a period of one year" [Act 9/2026 §25].

- The licence must also "specify the date of expiry" and is subject to an annual licence fee [Act 9/2026 §25].
- Different rule for microfinance business licences: a licence "shall be issued for a period of three years" [Act 9/2026 §32(7)], and again three years for a licensed microfinance institution [Act 9/2026 §32(9)].

Caveats: this is the Act as certified, not the bill; the question does not say which licence type you mean, and the two durations differ. Section 25's opening words cross-refer to sections 23–24, so read the one-year period as applying to those moneylending licences.

question: How far in advance must a container depot operator lodge a renewal request before the current licence ends?
answer:
Under the Licensing of Container Depot Operators Act, No. 3 of 2026, the renewal application must be submitted "not less than thirty days prior to the date of expiration" of the current licence [Act 3/2026 §6].

- The application must be in the prescribed Form and accompanied by the prescribed renewal fee [Act 3/2026 §6].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, what is the new maximum duration a freezing order may be in effect?
answer:
Under the Prevention of Money Laundering (Amendment) Act, No. 16 of 2026, the maximum period is raised from three months to **four months** ("shall not exceed four months") [Act 16/2026 §9(2)(a)].

- The same clause also substitutes "a period of three years" for "a period of two years", but the extract does not state what that longer period governs [Act 16/2026 §9(2)(a)].
- Separately, a police-issued Freezing Order runs "for a period of fourteen working days" (up from seven days) [Act 16/2026 §8(3)].

Caveats: This is an amending Act, so the amended section 8 text itself is not in the evidence; the description of the two/three-year change is incomplete.

question: Under the amended Telecommunication Levy law, how often is the levy calculated on the value of telecom services received?
answer:
Monthly: the substituted section 2 charges the levy "on the value of the supply of telecommunication services provided by any operator or provider, on the receipt of such telecommunication services in respect of each month" [028/2026 §2].

- The same clause text appears in the 2026-05-06 Bill [035/2026; §2 text identical per 028/2026 §2], whose Gazette text is dated 2026-04-23.
- Rates are set in the new Schedule, not in section 2 itself [028/2026 §2].

Caveats: This is a proposed amendment, not shown to have passed — no certified Act is held (Acts checked to 2026-10-30); the earlier 2015 and 2011 texts used the same "each month" formula [006/2015 §2; 011/2011 §2].

question: Under the amended Bills of Exchange Ordinance, what ways are allowed for informing a party that a bill has been refused or not paid?
answer:
Act No. 13 of 2025 (certified 2025-08-15) substitutes section 49(5) of the Bills of Exchange Ordinance, allowing notice of dishonour to be given "in writing or by personal communication, or by facsimile transmission or other electronic means" [Act 13/2025 §8].

- The electronic or facsimile means must "sufficiently identify the bill, and intimate that the bill has been dishonoured by non-acceptance or non-payment" [Act 13/2025 §8].
- This is an amending Act, so it states the substituted wording rather than the Ordinance's full current text [Act 13/2025 §8].

Caveats: The evidence shows only the new subsection (5); other parts of section 49 are not reproduced.

question: Under the proposed Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation incorporation law, who is defined as a qualified auditor?
answer:
In the newest bill — Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation (Incorporation), Bill of 2025-07-23 (also identical in 607/2025) — §11(4) defines a "qualified auditor" as either an individual, or a firm of accountants, meeting the Institute membership and practising-certificate tests. This is a bill only: no certified Act is held, so it has not been shown to have passed.

- Individual: a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka "or any other Institute established by law" who "possesses a certified to practice as Accountant issued by the Council of such Institute" [626/2025 §11(4)(a)].
- Firm: "a firm of Accountants each of the resident partners, of which being a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka or of any other Institute established by law possesses a certificate to practice as Accountant issued by the Council of such Institute" [626/2025 §11(4)(b)].
- The audit itself "shall be audited by a qualified auditor appointed by Auditor General" [626/2025 §11(3)].

An earlier Bill, 544/2024 (2024-08-08), carries the same definition but allowed audit by the Auditor General or a qualified auditor appointed by the Auditor General [544/2024 §11(3)].

Caveats: The 2025 text reads "certified to practice" (sic) rather than "certificate".

question: What is meant by “knowledge sharing activities” under the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture Act?
answer:
The only definition in the evidence is in a bill, not an Act: the Gazette text defines it as “activities designed to facilitate to exchange of ideas, skills, and experiences fostering on culture of learning and collaboration” [646/2025 §18].

- Source: Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture (Incorporation) bill, Gazette text of 2025-11-20 (same text in 002/2026) [646/2025 §18].
- It appears in the interpretation clause, so it governs how the term is read throughout that bill [646/2025 §18].

Caveats: No certified Act is held for this bill, so this wording is a proposal and has not been shown to have passed; the quoted phrase reproduces the text’s own wording.

question: According to the proposed Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka law, what authority does the Society have to obtain and manage real or personal assets, and what actions may it take with those assets?
answer:
The Bill would let the Society "take and hold any property, movable or immovable" and hold it for the Act's purposes, subject to its section 7 rules, "with power to sell, mortgage, lease, exchange, or otherwise dispose of the same" [047/2026 §13]. This is a bill, not law (no certified Act held).

- It may "purchase, rent construct, renovate and otherwise obtain lands or buildings" and deal with or dispose of them as the Council determines [047/2026 §6(a)].
- It may administer "any lawful trust" or "any real or personal property" to promote its objects [047/2026 §6(f)].
- Rules made under section 7 must cover "the administration and management of the property of the body corporate" [047/2026 §7(1)(f)].

Caveats: The Gazette text (2026-06-11) carries the same wording [041/2026 §13, §6]; the later Bill (2026-06-25) is cited.

question: In the Institute of Real Estate Professionals, who chairs the Membership and Policy Advisory committees, and how are chairs selected for the remaining committees?
answer:
Under the Act, the President of the Institute chairs both named committees; other committees are chaired by a Council member appointed to them. This is from Act No. 6/2026 (certified 2026-02-19), not the bill.

- The committees are the "Membership Committee" and the "Policy Advisory and Constitutional Committee", and "the President of the Institute shall be the Chairperson" of both [Act 6/2026 §18(1)(a)-(b), §18(2)].
- Every other committee must include "at least, one member of the Council and such member shall be the Chairperson" [Act 6/2026 §18(2)].
- If more than one Council member sits on a committee, "the Council shall appoint one of such members as the Chairperson" [Act 6/2026 §18(3)].

Caveats: the Act does not name the individual holding the office of President; the Gazette text said "Chairman" where the Act says "Chairperson" [637/2025 §18(2)].

question: Under the amended Colombo Port City Economic Commission law, how is the income tax treatment of workers hired by licensed businesses affected depending on whether the licence was granted before or after the new provisions take effect?
answer:
Under the certified Act, the dividing line is the date the new section 35 commences: employees of businesses licensed *before* that date get a three-year income tax exemption, while employees of businesses licensed *on or after* it are taxable [Act 1/2026 §3].

- Pre-commencement licensees: for "a period of three years commencing from the month immediately following the month in which this section comes into operation", resident employees' employment income is exempt and treated as a permissible credit to a personal foreign currency account; non-resident employees' income is exempt and they are not liable on income earned outside Sri Lanka [Act 1/2026 §3 §35(2)].
- Post-commencement licensees: "Any employment income of a resident employee and a non-resident employee ... shall be liable to income tax" [Act 1/2026 §3 §35(3)].

Caveats: this is an amending Act substituting section 35 of the 2021 Act, not the consolidated text; the earlier bills (652/2025, 654/2025) contained the same scheme but were only proposals [654/2025 §3].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators Act, how is the Act’s long title changed regarding the mention of container operators?
answer:
Under the certified Act, section 2 amends the 1972 Act's long title by substituting "freight forwArders And non-VesseL operAting common cArriers" for "freight forwArders, non-VesseL operAting common cArriers, And contAiner operAtors" — i.e. the words "and container operators" are dropped [Act 4/2026 §2].

- This is Act No. 4 of 2026 (certified 2026-02-17), not a bill; the same wording appeared in bill 005/2026 [Act 4/2026 §2].
- Relatedly, §3 replaces the Act's name generally with "Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders and Non-Vessel Operating Common Carriers Act" [Act 4/2026 §3].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, what modification is being made to the existing law?
answer:
The amendment is now law, not a bill: the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing (Amendment) Act, No. 18 of 2026 (certified 2026-08-04, from bills 018/2026 and 029/2026) amends Act No. 25 of 2005 on many fronts — widening the definitions of what may be frozen/forfeited, extending extraterritorial reach, adding new offences, and lengthening the freezing-order period.

- A Schedule substitutes "funds, property or other assets, material support or resources" for "funds or property" and similar phrases in listed sections [Act 18/2026 p.18].
- In section 4(3) the words "seven days" are replaced by "fourteen working days" [Act 18/2026 §5].
- Section 3 no longer requires proof that funds "were actually used", and adds offences of organising/directing, acting as accomplice and conspiring to collect or provide funds; section 16A inserts definitions including "foreign terrorist fighter" [Act 18/2026 §4, §16].

Caveats: only excerpts are in evidence, so this is not a full list of changes, and the current text of the 2005 Act is not included.

question: Which 2025 bill outlines the government's budget and borrowing provisions for the financial year 2026?
answer:
The Appropriation Bill — presented 2025-09-26 as bills 632/2025 and 639/2025 — is the one; it became **Appropriation Act, No. 23 of 2025** (certified 2025-12-05), so the law is the Act, not the bill [639/2025 §2] [Act 23/2025 §2].

- The Act authorises estimated expenditure of Rs 4,434,356,468,000 for the period 1 Jan–31 Dec 2026, and borrowing with an outstanding balance capped at Rs 3,740 billion, loan details going into the Final Budget Position Report under s.51 of the Public Financial Management Act, No. 44 of 2024 [Act 23/2025 §2(1)].
- Wording difference: the bill set the borrowing cap at Rs 3,800 billion; the Act reduced it to Rs 3,740 billion [639/2025 §2(1)] [Act 23/2025 §2(1)].

Caveats: the bills' text is pre-enactment; other 2025 bills may share similar appropriation boilerplate, but no other matching bill appears in the evidence.

question: What 2026 legislation establishes a new foundation to promote economic growth and rural resource development in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The best match is the **Economic and Rural Resources Development Foundation (Incorporation)** bill — 2026-07-27 presented version [055/2026] and the earlier Gazette text of 2026-06-15 [043/2026], titled to "incorporate the Economic and Rural Resources Development Foundation" [043/2026 p.2]. It has **not been shown to have passed**: no certified Act is held (Acts checked to 2026-10-30), so it remains a proposal.

- It would make the Foundation a body corporate whose objects include developing "all economic sectors in Sri Lanka" and rural youth vocational training [043/2026 §3(1)(a)–(b)].
- Objects also cover micro-entrepreneurship for unemployed women/marginalised groups and soil conservation [043/2026 §3(1)(g), (i)].
- Rules require a two-thirds majority of members present and voting, and must be gazetted and laid before Parliament [043/2026 §7(1), (3)–(4)].

Caveats: the 055/2026 title spells "Recourses"; no penalties are set out.

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media law, what is the maximum length of a suspension the Council can impose instead of disenrolling a member?
answer:
Under Bill 054/2026, titled the **Establishment of the Chartered Institute of Media** (not exactly “Chartered Institute of Media law”), the maximum suspension is **one year**: the Council may “suspend him from membership for such period not exceeding one year” instead of disenrolling [054/2026 §24].

- This applies where the Disciplinary Committee’s report establishes “professional misconduct” [054/2026 §24].
- The text is a **bill**, not shown to have passed; no certified Act is held [054/2026 §24].

question: Under the Protection of Occupants Bill, how long must someone have continuously and peacefully occupied a premises to be regarded as an “occupant”?
answer:
More than three months: a person must be in lawful occupation and have been in "undisturbed and uninterrupted occupation" for "a period of more than three months" before the events in sections 3–5, to be an "occupant" [004/2026 §2].

- The newest text is Bill 004/2026 (Bill, 2026-01-20); the earlier Gazette text 634/2025 (2025-09-18) uses the same three-month, undisturbed-and-uninterrupted wording [634/2025 §2].
- The words "peacefully" appear only in an auto-generated summary, not in the clause text, which says "undisturbed and uninterrupted" [004/2026 §2].

Caveats: Both are proposals; no certified Act is held, so this has not been shown to have passed [004/2026 §2].

question: Under the proposed Gambling Regulatory Authority law, what is the age limit beyond which a person cannot serve on the Authority's Board?
answer:
Under the Gambling Regulatory Authority Act, No. 17 of 2025 (certified 2025-09-03), a person "over seventy years of age" is disqualified from appointment to the Board — so the limit is 70.

- Disqualification is listed among other grounds, e.g. being a member of Parliament or an undischarged insolvent [Act 17/2025 §9(i)].
- The Act is now law, not a bill: it came from bills 594/2025 and 613/2025 [Act 17/2025 §9].
- Board tenure is separate: three years, with up to two re-appointments [Act 17/2025 §10].

Caveats: the clause bars appointment of someone already over 70; it does not spell out removal upon reaching 70 while in office.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, what is the longest jail term a person can receive for arriving in or departing Sri Lanka with cash or bearer‑negotiable instruments above the minister‑set limit?
answer:
One year's imprisonment — the substituted section 27 makes the offence punishable by a fine of up to three times the value of the cash or instruments, or "imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding one year", or both [Act 17/2026 §31].

- The limit is the sum the Minister specifies by Order published in the Gazette under the Foreign Exchange Act, No. 12 of 2017 [Act 17/2026 §31].
- Excess cash or instruments are also forfeited to the State [Act 17/2026 §31].

This is from the Financial Transactions Reporting (Amendment) Act, No. 17 of 2026 (certified 2026-08-04), an amending Act that repeals and substitutes section 27 of the principal enactment; the amended Act's full current text is not in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Sri Lanka Cricket law, what penalty amount does a member owe if they fail to pay the subscription by the deadline?
answer:
Under the proposed law, the defaulting member owes a "late payment fee equal to twice the annual subscription" [072/2026 §30(4)].

- The subscription itself is due by 31 December of the preceding year [072/2026 §30(3)]; the doubled fee is payable by 30 April of the following year [072/2026 §30(4)].
- Failing that, voting rights are automatically forfeited [072/2026 §30(5)], and removal from the Register follows after six months [072/2026 §30(6)].

Caveats: this is the Gazette text of a bill (Sri Lanka Cricket), not shown to have passed [072/2026 §30].

question: Under the proposed Indira Cancer Charitable Trust Act, on which day must the newly formed body corporate settle the Trust's existing debts and liabilities?
answer:
The evidence does not give a settlement day. [009/2026 §12] only fixes *which* debts and liabilities the body corporate must pay: those "existing on the day immediately preceding the date of commencement of this Act" — so the cut-off is the day before commencement, not a deadline for payment.

- The same clause makes debts due, subscriptions and contributions payable to the Trust on that day payable to the body corporate for the Act's purposes [009/2026 §12].
- This is a Gazette text of a bill (2026-02-05); no certified Act is held, so it has not been shown to have passed [009/2026 §12]. An earlier, differently titled bill, Indira Cancer Trust (Incorporation) (2021-08-23), carries identical wording [095/2021 §12].

Caveats: No payment deadline is stated in the passage; I cannot supply one.

question: Under the proposed Immigration Bill, what is the minimum and maximum penalty imposed on a ship's master or aircraft captain who fails to report a transit passenger or crew member that appears to have stayed in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Under the Immigration Bill (082/2026, dated 2026-10-07), the fine is a minimum of one hundred thousand rupees and a maximum of five hundred thousand rupees [082/2026 §90].

- Failure to notify an Immigration Officer of such a transit passenger or crew member is the offence, and the master, captain or agent is "jointly and severally liable" on conviction [082/2026 §90(1)–(2)].

Caveats: This is a bill, not law — no certified Act is held for it, so it has not been shown to have passed. Identical text appears in 508/2024, 513/2024 and 071/2026 [082/2026 §90].

question: Under the proposed Convention against Doping in Sport amendment, how long does the Board Chairman serve?
answer:
The Chairman of the Board holds office **for a term of three years** and is eligible for reappointment [Act 21/2025 §11].

- This appears in the certified Act, No. 21 of 2025 (certified 2025-10-07), which amends the Convention against Doping in Sport Act, No. 33 of 2013 — it substitutes new subsections for section 14(1) and (2) [Act 21/2025 §11].
- The Chairman is one of the two appointed members, chosen by the Minister on the recommendation of the majority of ex-officio members [Act 21/2025 §11].

Caveats: The evidence gives only the amending Act, not the consolidated text of the principal enactment; the three-year term is stated in the substituted subsection (2).

question: Under the amended Rubber Control Act, who is defined as the “Director‑General”?
answer:
Under the Rubber Control (Amendment) Act No. 16 of 2025 (certified 22 Aug 2025), “Director-General” means “the Director-General of the Rubber Development Department, appointed or deemed to have been appointed under this Act” [Act 16/2025 §6].

- The Act inserts this definition by repealing the “Controller” definition in section 52 of the principal enactment [Act 16/2025 §6].
- References to “Controller”/“Rubber Controller” are replaced with “Director-General,” and external documents are read as referring to the “Director-General of the Rubber Development Department” [Act 16/2025 §2].

Caveats: This is an amending Act; it states the change, not the consolidated text of the amended Act.

question: In the amended Personal Data Protection Act, which bodies are regarded as a public authority?
answer:
Under the amendment made by Act 22/2025, “public authority” means “a Ministry, any Department, Provincial Council, local authority, or a Ministry or Department of a Provincial Council”, excluding a public corporation and a company incorporated under the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007 [Act 22/2025 §14(2)].

- The exclusion of public corporations and Companies Act companies is express — the opposite of the earlier proposal, which included public corporations, statutory bodies and government-majority companies [152/2021 §47].
- This is an amendment substituting the definition in the principal Act (No. 9 of 2022); the amended Act's consolidated text is not in the evidence [Act 22/2025 §14].

Caveats: only the amending clause is available and it is shown truncated at the exclusion list; the verified full wording of the substituted definition should be checked against the principal Act as amended.

question: What criteria does the amendment set for a crop to be classified as an Export Agricultural Crop?
answer:
Under the certified Act 24/2026, a crop qualifies only if it has “an export potential in addition to the local consumption”, is outside the excluded food-crop list and is not a plantation crop, and the Minister declares it a “notified agricultural crop” under section 2 [Act 24/2026 §5].

- Expressly excluded: “paddy, vegetables, fruits, root crops and additional food crops belonging to the category of food crops”, and “any crop identified as a plantation crop” [Act 24/2026 §5].
- The definition is substituted into section 19 of the Promotion of Export Agriculture Act, No. 46 of 1992 [Act 24/2026 §5].

Caveats: the amended 1992 Act's full text is not in evidence; the above is the new definition as drafted in the amending Act.

question: Under the proposed Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka law, what does the term “qualified auditor” refer to?
answer:
It means either an individual, or a firm whose resident partners are, members of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (or another institute established by law) holding a certificate to practise as an Accountant issued by that institute's Council — defined in the audit clause of the Chiththa bill [597/2025 §10(4)].

- Two limbs: "an individual who, being a member… possesses a certificate to practice as an Accountant" [597/2025 §10(4)(a)]; or "a firm of Accountants each of the resident partners of which" meets the same test [597/2025 §10(4)(b)].
- The auditor is appointed by the Auditor General under Article 154 of the Constitution [597/2025 §10(3)].

Caveats: This is the Gazette text of a bill (29 May 2025; also in Bill 608/2025, 6 June 2025) and has not been shown to have passed, so it is not law; no certified Act is held.

question: Under the proposed Proceeds of Crime Bill, what types of advanced investigative methods can an investigation officer employ with a magistrate’s permission?
answer:
The bill is now law: the Proceeds of Crime Act, No. 5 of 2025 (certified 2025-04-30), which calls these "special investigative techniques" — the bill's phrase "advanced investigative techniques" was not enacted [570/2025 §60 §STATUS].

- On a Magistrate's authorisation under s.56, an investigation officer may use "controlled delivery", "digital surveillance" (interception/recording of digital, voice and video communication), "undercover operations including those involving the use of decoys", "laying of traps", and "forensic extraction of data, information and images" from computers, phones and digital devices [Act 5/2025 §60(1)].
- The Magistrate weighs "necessity and justification" on "the principle of proportionality", and progress must be reported "once in fourteen days" [Act 5/2025 §60(3), (4)].
- Separately, a judicial order can compel forensic audit, digital forensic extraction, property valuation, data copying/storage and forensic transaction analysis [Act 5/2025 §61].

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka law, how many council members must be present, and must the Chairperson be among them, to constitute a quorum for a council meeting?
answer:
Five members, including the Chairperson: the quorum for any Council meeting "shall be five members including the Chairperson" [040/2026 §7(2)].

- The same wording appears in the later Bill version, titled "Establishment of the Chartered Institute of Media" [054/2026 §7(2)] — near-identical text under a slightly different title.
- If the Chairperson is absent, the Vice-Chairperson presides, but the quorum figure itself still requires the Chairperson [040/2026 §7(5)(b)].

Caveat: both are proposals only; no certified Act was found (Acts checked to 2026-10-30), so this has not been shown to have passed.

question: Under the National Transport Commission amendment, what steps must the Commission and transport operators follow to set and show fares for bus and other transport services?
answer:
Under Act 8/2025 §19 (certified 2025-06-20), which inserts s.38A into the National Transport Commission Act, the Commission sets fares by formula and publishes them; operators must then display their own fare list on the vehicle. Note this is an amending Act, so the requirement is a new section, not the full current text of the principal Act.

- Setting: the Commission computes fares for services "including omnibus services" by a formula it determines from time to time, "in accordance with the national policy relating to transportation fares approved by Parliament", specified by Order published in the Gazette [Act 8/2025 §19].
- Publication: the Commission publishes fare lists for the respective services on its official website [Act 8/2025 §19].
- Showing: each provider prepares its list "in accordance with such lists published in such website" and it "shall be displayed in a conspicuous place of the transportation vehicle"; the Commission may inspect compliance and failure is an offence under s.40 [Act 8/2025 §19].

Caveats: the penalty and the s.39/s.40 inspection provisions are not reproduced in the evidence, so amounts can't be stated; no fare-registration or terminal-display duty appears in the evidence.

question: According to the proposed Mass Foundation law, what continuous legal identity will the foundation have, what ability does it have to bring or face lawsuits, how can it manage its seal, and how is it classified for regulatory oversight?
answer:
The Mass Foundation would be a body corporate with “perpetual succession” under the name “Mass Foundation” and may “sue and be sued”; this is a proposal in the Gazette text of 8 April 2026 (identical in the Bill of 7 May 2026), not shown to have passed [025/2026 §2].

- It may “have and use a common seal and … alter the same at its pleasure” [025/2026 §2].
- The seal may be affixed only in the presence of two Committee members, who must sign independently of any witness; custody lies with an office bearer chosen by the Committee [025/2026 §15].
- It is deemed a Voluntary Social Service Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980, whose provisions apply to its management [025/2026 §2].

question: Under the amendment to the National Water Supply and Drainage Board Law, when a water supply and sewerage undertaking of an industrial park is transferred to the Board, which minister is treated as the ‘Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government’ for applying Part III of the Act?
answer:
Under section 57A inserted by the National Water Supply and Drainage Board (Amendment) Act, No. 20 of 2026 (certified 2026-08-18), for an industrial estate or industrial park the words “the Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government” are read as “the Minister assigned the subject of the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka … or the Minister assigned the subject of industries …” under Article 44 or 45, “as the case may be” [Act 20/2026 §10].

- That reference is to the BOI Minister or the industries Minister, not the local government Minister [Act 20/2026 §10, proviso (a)].
- A separate rule applies to community based organisations: the Minister assigned community based water supply [Act 20/2026 §10, proviso (b)].

Caveats: this is an amending Act, not the consolidated Law; the text does not say how to choose between the two Ministers if both subjects are assigned. The identical wording appeared in the earlier bill [019/2026 §10], which is not law.

question: Under the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, what responsibilities does a magistrate have when an approved detention centre lies within his jurisdiction?
answer:
Under the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill (2026-10-06), the magistrate must act without advance notice to the detention authority.

- Visit the approved detention centre **once a month**, interview suspects and look into their well-being, and inspect detention registers, Detention Orders and other required documents [078/2026 §33(1)].
- If torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment is observed or alleged, **forthwith** order the suspect’s production for examination by a Judicial Medical Officer and submission of the report [078/2026 §33(4)].
- The centre’s authority must give the magistrate prompt, unimpeded access [078/2026 §33(3)].

Caveats: This is a bill, not shown to have passed; identical text appears in the Gazette text of 2026-09-22 [070/2026 §33].

question: Under the Mediation (Civil and Commercial Disputes) Bill, which civil or commercial disagreements can be taken to mediation and which types are excluded from this law?
answer:
The Bill is now **Act No. 13 of 2026** (certified 30 June 2026, from bills 616/2025 and 622/2025), so I answer from the Act: it applies to "civil and commercial disputes" settled by mediation — under a mediation agreement, by voluntary referral, or by court referral [Act 13/2026 §2(1)]; the schedule lists the excluded categories [Act 13/2026 §30].

- Excluded entirely: disputes required to go to mediation under the Mediation Boards Act, No. 72 of 1988 or the Mediation (Special Categories of Disputes) Act, No. 21 of 2003 [Act 13/2026 §2(2)–(3)].
- Not mediable: disputes needing terms enforceable "only on a decree or order of court", including the scheduled matters — divorce and nullity, persons of unsound mind/minors/wards, guardians and receivers, adoption, births and deaths registration, partition for rights in rem, probate and letters of administration, insolvency relief, admiralty rights in rem, and fundamental-rights breaches [Act 13/2026 §3; §30]. Related matters may still be mediated to produce settlement terms for court [Act 13/2026 §3].

Caveats: the schedule text appears only in the §30 passage; the Act does not otherwise define "civil and commercial".

question: What audit regulations govern the financial statements of Samurdhi community‑based banking societies under the Samurdhi amendment?
answer:
Under the Samurdhi (Amendment) Act, No. 15 of 2025 (certified 2025-08-22), the accounts of samurdhi community‑based **banking societies** must be audited under the public‑corporation audit regime and the National Audit Act.

- New section 35A of the Samurdhi Act, No. 1 of 2013 applies "the provisions of Article 154 of the Constitution relating to audit of accounts of public corporations and the provisions of the National Audit Act, No. 19 of 2018" to those societies' audit [Act 15/2025 §3].
- The companion new section 28A applies the same rules to "samurdhi community based banks" (a different class of body) [Act 15/2025 §2].

Caveats: This is an amending Act; it states the change, not the consolidated text of the Samurdhi Act. The bill versions (600/2025, 614/2025) became this Act, so the Act is relied on.

question: Under the proposed Companies (Amendment) Act, what remedy is available to a company whose name has been struck off, and what are the effects on its former assets?
answer:
The remedy is in the certified Act: a struck-off company may apply to court, with the Attorney-General made a party, within ten years of the Act's operation, and the court may permit re-registration and order return of the property that had vested in the State [Act 12/2025 §17].

- The company must "show cause to the satisfaction of the court" why it could not comply with subsection (1); the court may hold an inquiry [Act 12/2025 §17].
- Third-party rights acquired in good faith from the State over property already "dealt with or disposed of" are unaffected [Act 12/2025 §17].
- Where property was destroyed, damaged, or never taken into the State's physical possession, "the State shall not be liable to any party in any manner" [Act 12/2025 §17].

Caveats: This amends s.487(5) of the principal enactment, whose full text is not in the evidence; the identical proposal in bill 582/2025 (Gazette text) is not law, and the Act's wording governs.

question: Under the revised Anti‑Corruption Act, in what situations will a person charged with a corruption offence be refused bail?
answer:
The evidence does not show the enacted bail-refusal rule: the only bail wording is a **proposed** substitution for section 149(1), which the STATUS says was "not enacted in these words" [063/2026 §17].

- As proposed, all offences would be "cognizable and non-bailable", with no bail "except in exceptional circumstances by a High Court" where the bribe is "not less than one hundred thousand rupees" or the loss or benefit is "not less than five hundred thousand rupees", confirmed by a Director-General's certificate [051/2026 §17].
- The earlier Gazette text of section 149 required remand until the end of trial, with bail only in "exceptional circumstances and for reasons to be recorded" — but that too is a proposal, not law [311/2023 §149].

Caveats: The enacted text of the Anti-Corruption Act, No. 9 of 2023 (as amended by Act 25/2026), including any bail provision, is not in the evidence; Act 25/2026's summary mentions no bail change.

question: Under the proposed Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters law, how are offences listed in Part B of the extradition schedule treated when Sri Lanka considers extraditing a suspect to another UN member state?
answer:
Under the Gazette text of the proposed Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters bill, such offences are deemed **not** to be offences of a political character (nor connected with or inspired by political motives) for extradition purposes between Sri Lanka and any UN Member State — so the political-offence bar would not apply [073/2026 §11].

- This applies "for the purposes only of extradition" of a person accused or convicted of such an offence, or of affording assistance to a UN Member State under clause 12 [073/2026 §11].
- The deeming covers offences specified in Part B of the Extradition Law's Schedule "and this Act", notwithstanding the Extradition Law, No. 8 of 1977 [073/2026 §11].
- A related clause inserts a new item immediately before Part B covering "an offence within the meaning of" this Act [073/2026 §8].

Caveats: this is a Gazette text proposal only (identical text in 085/2026); it has not been shown to have passed, and we hold no certified Act for it.

question: Under the revised National Environmental Act, what monetary penalty does a person face if convicted of an offence covered by Section 23r, and what extra daily charge applies if the violation persists after the conviction?
answer:
Under the certified National Environmental (Amendment) Act No. 15 of 2026, the substituted Section 23r(2) sets a fine of **not less than Rs. 100,000 and not more than Rs. 1,000,000** on conviction before the Magistrate having jurisdiction [Act 15/2026 §18].

- If the offence continues after conviction, an additional fine of **Rs. 5,000 for each day** it continues after conviction applies [Act 15/2026 §18].

Caveat: this is an amending Act, so the quoted wording is the substituted provision, not a consolidated text of the principal Act [Act 15/2026 §18].

question: What penalty does the amendment to the National Audit Act impose for the offence covered by Section 42?
answer:
The National Audit (Amendment) Act, No. 19 of 2025 (certified 2025-09-22) substitutes for section 42's penalty "a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees or to an imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding one year or to both such fine and imprisonment" [Act 19/2025 §13].

- It replaces the earlier wording "to a fine not less than five thousand rupees and not more than twenty five thousand rupees" [Act 19/2025 §13].
- Do not confuse this with section 43, amended separately to allow imprisonment "not exceeding three year" [Act 19/2025 §14].

Caveats: This is an amending Act; the consolidated text of section 42 is not in the evidence. The 2018 Gazette proposal of section 42 showed a different penalty (six months) [421/2018 §42], but it is only a proposal and not checked against the enacted 2018 Act.

question: Under the proposed Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs law, what fine and additional action apply if a dog owner does not vaccinate and register the dog after being given a notice?
answer:
Under the proposal, failure to vaccinate and register within the notice period makes the person liable to a penalty of "two thousand rupees in addition to the registration fee payable under section 5", and the local authority must itself vaccinate and register the dog [076/2026 §7(4)].

- The notice period is fourteen days, extendable by a further fourteen days on reasonable cause [076/2026 §7(2)–(3)].
- The dog is then entered immediately in the "Register of Dogs" kept under section 8 [076/2026 §7(4)]; [066/2026 §8].

Caveats: This is a bill, not law — Bill 076/2026 (2026-09-24), same wording as the Gazette text 066/2026 (2026-09-07); no certified Act is held, so it has not been shown to have passed.

question: Under the proposed amendment to Sri Lanka’s drug control law, how is the list of named narcotics changed and what new penalty is introduced for manufacturing other listed dangerous drugs?
answer:
It is an amending Act (Act 27/2026, certified 2026-10-30, formerly bill 068/2026), not the Ordinance's current text. Under it, section 54A(1)(a) of the Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs Ordinance substitutes "heroin, cocaine, morphine, opium or methamphetamine" for the earlier words naming only heroin, cocaine, morphine or opium [Act 27/2026 §2].

- New offence: manufacturing a dangerous drug in Groups A–E, Part I, Third Schedule, "other than heroin, cocaine, morphine, opium and methamphetamine" [Act 27/2026 §2(2)].
- Penalty: on conviction by the High Court without a jury, a fine "not less than two hundred thousand rupees and not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees", or 10–20 years' imprisonment, or both [Act 27/2026 §2(2)].

Caveats: The separate Third Schedule amendment (cannabis entries) appears in the outline but its text is not in the evidence, so the schedule's new wording cannot be confirmed [Act 27/2026; 068/2026].

question: Under the proposed Presidents' Entitlements repeal, will former presidents or their widows keep receiving housing, regular payments, secretarial assistance, official transport or a widow's pension once the new law takes effect?
answer:
No. Under the Presidents' Entitlements (Repeal) Act, No. 18 of 2025 (certified 2025-09-10), those benefits stop from the date the Act commences.

- Residence and monthly allowance previously given to a former President or a former President's widow "shall no longer be provided with or paid to" on and after commencement [Act 18/2025 §3(a)].
- Same for the "monthly secretarial allowance", "official transport and such other facilities" [Act 18/2025 §3(b)], and the widow's "monthly pension" [Act 18/2025 §3(c)].
- The repeal of the 1986 Act (No. 4 of 1986) is effected by §2 [Act 18/2025 §2].

Caveats: This is a certified Act, not a bill — the 2025 bills (624/2025, 627/2025) became Act 18/2025; the Act's own text governs. The text covers benefits received "preceding the date of commencement", so it does not address any separate scheme outside the repealed Act.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Penal Code, what new penalty is introduced for intentionally causing serious injury to a child under 18?
answer:
The proposal would insert a new Penal Code section 316a: "voluntarily causes grievous hurt to a person under eighteen years of age" is punishable by up to ten years' imprisonment, plus a fine and possible compensation — but this is a bill (Penal Code (Amendment), Gazette text 2025-07-08, also in the 2025-08-19 Bill), not law.

- Term: "imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years" [618/2025 §6].
- Also "liable to fine" and may be ordered to pay compensation, fixed by court after a victim impact statement from the National Authority for the Protection of Victims of Crime and Witnesses [618/2025 §6].

Caveats: The text says "voluntarily causes grievous hurt", not "intentionally"; no certified Act is held, so it has not been shown to have passed.

question: How does the proposed amendment to the Social Security Contribution Levy Act change the turnover limits and the applicable dates in Section 5, and what new limit is introduced for periods starting on 1 April 2026?
answer:
The evidence does not support a limit for periods starting 1 April 2026: that date appears only in the Gazette bill, which was changed before enactment. The Act as certified uses **1 July 2026** and sets a new four-quarter turnover ceiling of **thirty-six million rupees**.

- Proposed (Gazette text, 2026-03-03): paragraph (c) limited to "on or after January 1, 2024 and prior to April 1, 2026", with new paragraph (d) for periods "commencing on or after April 1, 2026" capped at "thirty-six million rupees" [017/2026 §3] — a proposal only, not law.
- Enacted (Act No. 10/2026, certified 2026-04-09): paragraph (c) reads "on or after January 1, 2024 and prior to July 1, 2026", and new paragraph (d) applies to "any period commencing on or after July 1, 2026" with the same "thirty-six million rupees" limit [Act 10/2026 §3].
- Paragraph (b)'s "hundred and twenty million rupees; or" became "hundred and twenty million rupees;" (i.e. "or" dropped, so (c) follows on) [Act 10/2026 §3].

Caveats: The bill's April 1, 2026 date was not enacted in those words; the evidence does not show the current consolidated text of section 5, since an amending Act only states changes.

question: What changes does the amendment to Section 14 of the Sri Lanka Electricity Act make to the ownership percentage requirement and to the type of entities mentioned in its subsections?
answer:
The certified Sri Lanka Electricity (Amendment) Act, No. 14 of 2025 amends Section 14 of the principal Act by replacing “more than fifty per centum” with “one hundred per centum” in subsection (1) [Act 14/2025 §12].

- In subsection (2), “Any person who” is replaced by “Any company incorporated in terms of the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007, which” [Act 14/2025 §12].
- In subsection (3), “a person who” is replaced by “a company, which” [Act 14/2025 §12].

Caveat: this is an amending Act, so it states the changes; the full amended text of the principal Act is not in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Trusts Ordinance, which part of Section 3 is being removed and how is the definition of “express trust” being changed?
answer:
The bill would repeal paragraph (n) of Section 3 of the Trusts Ordinance (Chapter 87) and, in paragraph (p), replace the words “trust generally in the form” in the definition of “express trust” with “trust in the form” [081/2026 §2].

- The amendment is to Section 3 “as last amended by Act, No. 6 of 2018” [081/2026 §2].
- This is the Gazette text of the Trusts (Amendment) bill dated 2026-10-14; it is a proposal, not shown to have passed (no certified Act held, Acts checked to 2026-10-30) [081/2026 §2].

Caveats: the content of the repealed paragraph (n) and the full definition are not in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Judicature Act, how are the retirement ages for judges and magistrates being changed?
answer:
Under the Judicature (Amendment) Act, No. 23 of 2026 (certified 2026-09-25, from bills 058/2026 and 064/2026), the retirement age in section 6(3) rises from 61 to 63, and section 6(4) is replaced so that "the age of retirement of all other Judges and Magistrates shall be sixty-two years" [Act 23/2026 §3].

- The 62-year age applies "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Public and Judicial Officers (Retirement) Ordinance (Chapter 355)" [Act 23/2026 §3(2)].
- This is an amending Act, so it states the changes only; the consolidated Judicature Act, No. 2 of 1978 text is not in the evidence [Act 23/2026 §3].

Caveats: The figures come from the certified Act, not the earlier bill versions.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Universities Act, how many terms is a person allowed to serve as dean of a faculty?
answer:
A person may serve no more than **two terms** as Dean of a Faculty — this is in the Universities (Amendment) Act, No. 2 of 2026 (certified 2026-02-03), which amends the Universities Act No. 16 of 1978 [Act 2/2026 §2].

- New subsection (4) of section 49: "No person shall be elected as the Dean of a Faculty for more than two terms" [Act 2/2026 §2(5)].
- This is law as passed, not a bill; the earlier Gazette text/bill 649/2025 & 655/2025 instead said "appointed as the Dean … for more than two terms", a wording change in the Act [649/2025 §2].

Caveats: the amended Universities Act's full text is not in evidence, so only the amendment's wording is stated.

question: What 2025 legislation establishes the professional facilities‑management institute as a legal corporate body in Sri Lanka?
answer:
No 2025 Act establishing it has been shown to have passed: the evidence holds only bills, not a certified Act (Acts checked up to 2026-10-30), for the Institute of Facilities Management Sri Lanka (Incorporation).

- The Gazette text of 2025-07-18 (623/2025 §2(1)) proposes that members "shall have perpetual succession under the name and style of the 'Institute of Facilities Management Sri Lanka'" and may "sue and be sued" with a common seal [623/2025 §2].
- The presented Bill version is 628/2025 (2025-08-06); its text is identical on this point [628/2025].
- Earlier 2024 bills (458/2024, 470/2024) carried the same incorporation clause [470/2024 §2].

Caveats: This is proposed wording, not law; no certified Act is in the evidence.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 470/2024 §2, 623/2025 §2

question: Which 2025 legislation creates a legal corporation for the charitable foundation named after senior monk Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero?
answer:
No 2025 Act is shown: the matching legislation is the **Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero Suwasevana Foundation (Incorporation)** bill — Bill 596/2025 (2025-05-08), an earlier Gazette text being 581/2025 (2025-04-10) — which is a proposal, not law [596/2025 §1][596/2025 §2][581/2025 §2].

- Its clause 2 would make the Foundation's members "a body corporate with perpetual succession", able to sue, be sued and use a common seal [596/2025 §2].
- Clause 1 gives the intended short title "... (Incorporation) Act, No. of 2025" [596/2025 §1].

Caveats: the evidence records no certified Act for this bill (Acts checked to 2026-10-30), so it has not been shown to have passed; the two versions' clause 2 wording is identical [596/2025 §2][581/2025 §2].

question: What 2026 amendment revises the Act that governs marriage and divorce among the Kandyan community (Chapter 113)?
answer:
The Kandyan Marriage and Divorce (Amendment) Bill, No. 008/2026 (Gazette text, 2026-02-05), later presented as Bill 016/2026 (2026-02-19), amends Chapter 113; neither has been shown to have passed — no certified Act is held for them.

- §2 substitutes section 32(a) with “Adultery by the husband or wife after marrige.” [008/2026 §2] (the spelling is as printed).
- §2 also repeals paragraph (b) of section 32 [008/2026 §2].
- Sinhala text to prevail on inconsistency [008/2026 §3].

Caveats: Both are proposals, not law; the summary's reference to "the Amendment Act" is auto-generated wording only.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 008/2026 §3

question: What is the 2026 legislation that establishes the Al‑Hashimi Association as a legal corporate entity?
answer:
The 2026 proposal is the **Al‑Hashimi Association (Incorporation)** bill — Gazette text 024/2026 (2026‑04‑08), later presented as Bill 039/2026 (2026‑05‑21). It has not been shown to have passed; no certified Act is held (Acts checked to 2026‑10‑30), so it is a bill, not law.

- §2(1) would give members "perpetual succession under the name and style of the 'Al‑Hashimi Association'", with power to sue, be sued and use a common seal [024/2026 §2].
- §2(2) deems it a Voluntary Social Service Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [024/2026 §2].
- Rules require a two‑thirds majority of members present and voting, and must be gazetted and laid before Parliament [024/2026 §7].

Caveats: the two versions appear to share identical clause text; nothing in the evidence shows enactment.

question: Which 2026 bill repeals the 2009 act that created the position of chief of the defence staff in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) Act, No. 22 of 2026 (certified 2026-09-22) repeals the Chief of Defence Staff Act, No. 35 of 2009 [Act 22/2026 §2].

- It began as bill 036/2026 (Gazette text, 2026-05-15) and 059/2026 (Bill, 2026-08-04); those are proposals, so the Act is the law [059/2026][036/2026].
- The repeal takes effect from commencement, when the Chief of Defence Staff and Committee members "cease to hold such office" [Act 22/2026 §3].

Caveats: The evidence gives the Act's repeal and transitional provisions but not the commencement date.

question: What 2025 legislation modifies the 1988 Provincial Councils Elections Act in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Two 2025 bills would amend the Provincial Councils Elections Act, No. 2 of 1988: Bill 589/2025 (Gazette text, 22 May 2025) and Bill 605/2025 (Bill, 5 June 2025), whose clause text is identical. Neither has been shown to have passed—no certified Act is held (Acts checked to 30 October 2026)—so this is proposed, not enacted, law.

- It restores the 1988 Act's provisions "in force on September 21, 2017 … notwithstanding the amendments made thereto by Act, No. 17 of 2017" [589/2025 §2].
- Acts done from 22 September 2017 to commencement are preserved "insofar as such act is not inconsistent with" the 1988 Act [589/2025 §2].
- Short title: "Provincial Councils Elections (Amendment) Act, No. of 2025" [589/2025 §1].

Caveats: 605/2025 adds the presenting MP (Shanakiyan Rajaputhiran Rasamanickam) [605/2025]; identical 2023 proposals exist but pre-date the question's year [322/2023 §3].

question: Which 2025 bill amends the 2016 Act that provides a financial assistance scheme for workers?
answer:
The 2025 bill is the **Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment)** bill — 602/2025 (presented 2025-06-03), preceded by Gazette text 587/2025 (2025-05-20), both amending the Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, No. 4 of 2016 [Act 10/2025 §2] [602/2025].

- It substitutes in section 3 of the 2016 Act periods ending "March 31, 2025" for the open-ended 2015 and 2016 start dates [Act 10/2025 §2].
- Both bills became **Act No. 10 of 2025** (certified 2025-07-23), deemed operative April 1, 2025 [Act 10/2025 §1] [602/2025].
- The Act's wording governs; the summary descriptions are auto-generated hints only [602/2025 §2].

Caveats: The 2016 Act's own text is not in the evidence, so only the changes are stated, not its current reading.

question: Which 2025 bill seeks to amend the 2016 legislation that establishes the minimum wage for employees in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Two: Bill 586/2025 (Gazette text, 20 May 2025) and Bill 604/2025 (Bill, 3 June 2025, the newer) — both titled National Minimum Wage of Workers (Amendment) and both amend the National Minimum Wage of Workers Act, No. 3 of 2016 [586/2025] [604/2025] [Act 11/2025 §2].

- Both became Act No. 11 of 2025 (certified 23 July 2025), so the law is the Act, not the bills [Act 11/2025 §1].
- The Act sets the monthly minimum at "twenty-seven thousand rupees" (daily 1,080) from 1 April 2025 to 31 December 2025, then "thirty thousand rupees" (daily 1,200) from 1 January 2026, deemed effective 1 April 2025 [Act 11/2025 §2] [Act 11/2025 §1(2)].

Caveats: The evidence does not include the Act's own text beyond §§1–3; the earlier 2016 Act's full text is not provided. The §2 wording in 604/2025 differs slightly from the Act — rely on the Act [604/2025 §2].

question: Which 2025 amendment alters the 2005 law that established the workers' special financial assistance allowance?
answer:
**Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment) Act, No. 9 of 2025**, certified 2025-07-23, amends the Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, No. 36 of 2005 [Act 9/2025 §2]. (The 2005 Act is described in the evidence as the Budgetary Relief Allowance law, not by the phrase "special financial assistance allowance".)

- It substituted "With effect from August 1, 2005" in section 3(1) with "For the period commencing on August 1, 2005 and ending on March 31, 2025" [Act 9/2025 §2].
- It came from bills 588/2025 (Gazette text, 2025-05-20) and 603/2025 (Bill, 2025-06-03), both now superseded by the Act [588/2025; 603/2025].
- Act 11/2025 (National Minimum Wage amendment) only refers to the 2005 Act when consolidating allowances; it does not amend it [Act 11/2025 §3].

question: What 2026 legislation proposes to abolish the 1977 law that provided retirement benefits to Sri Lankan parliamentarians?
answer:
The **Parliamentary Pensions (Repeal) Act, No. 5 of 2026** (certified 2026-02-17) — it repeals the Parliamentary Pensions Law, No. 1 of 1977 [Act 5/2026].

- It originated as bill 001/2026 (2026-01-07); the bill itself is a proposal only, and the Act is what became law [001/2026].
- From commencement, persons receiving a pension under the 1977 Law (or section 9 of Act No. 1 of 1982 / Act No. 47 of 1990) cease to receive it [Act 5/2026].
- On conflicting Sinhala and Tamil texts, the Sinhala text prevails [Act 5/2026 §4].

Caveats: The evidence gives only the outline of clauses 1–3 plus a summary; the full operative wording is not reproduced here.

question: Which 2025 bill sought to modify the 1988 Sri Lankan law that imposes a tax on gambling activities?
answer:
The **Betting and Gaming Levy (Amendment)** bill, which amends the Betting and Gaming Levy Act, No. 40 of 1988. It was published as bill 640/2025 (Gazette text, 2025-10-02) and presented as bill 642/2025 (Bill, 2025-10-21), with identical clause text [640/2025 §2] [642/2025 §2].

- It raised the rate from 15% to 18% and doubled a US$50 charge to US$100 [642/2025 §2].
- It became Act No. 25/2025 (certified 2025-12-17), but the enacted dates differ: 18% applies "on or after January 1, 2026", not October 1, 2025 [Act 25/2025 §2].

Caveats: The amending Act only states changes; the 1988 Act's full text is not in the evidence.

question: Which 2025 bill proposes changes to the Land Development Ordinance (Chapter 464)?
answer:
Bill 625/2025, the Land Development (Amendment) Bill (2025-07-22), presented by Hon. (Mrs.) Rohini Kumari Wijerathna, M.P., to amend the Land Development Ordinance (Chapter 464) [625/2025]. It is a bill, not law: no certified Act is held for it, so it has not been shown to have passed [625/2025 §1].

- It repeals "or upon his or her marriage" in subsection 48A 2(c) [625/2025 §2], repeals subsection 48B 1(a) [625/2025 §3], and substitutes "fails without reasonable cause to succeed" for "fails to succeed" in section 68(1) [625/2025 §4].
- The earlier Gazette text 617/2025 (2025-07-04) carries the same clauses [617/2025 §1, §3].

Caveats: Section 3's text also appears in 519/2024; the summaries are auto-generated hints only.

question: Which 2026 bill updates the 2018 Finance Act No. 35?
answer:
The Finance (Amendment) Bill 034/2026 (2026-05-06) amends the Finance Act, No. 35 of 2018; the same text appears in Bill 027/2026, its Gazette text of 2026-04-23 [034/2026 §2][027/2026].

- It substitutes section 44(1) to exempt a "newly constructed cellular tower" commencing commercial operations "on or after January 1, 2026" from the levy "for a period of five years" [034/2026 §2].
- It also amends section 44(2), making levy payment "Subject to the provisions of subsection (1)" [034/2026 §2].
- Both are proposals only; no certified Act is held, so neither has been shown to have passed [034/2026 §2].

Caveats: 034/2026 is a bill presented to Parliament; 027/2026 is the earlier Gazette text of the same amendment, not law.

question: Which 2026 bill revises the 1956 law that sets rules for female workers, teenage employees and child labor?
answer:
The 2026 bill is the **Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children (Amendment)** bill (056/2026, presented 2026-07-22), which became **Act No. 21 of 2026** (certified 2026-09-08); it amends the Act No. 47 of 1956 [Act 21/2026 §1][056/2026].

- Its stated purpose is "to Amend the employment of Women, young persons And children Act, no. 47 of 1956" [Act 21/2026 §1].
- In substance it substitutes "one hundred thousand rupees" for "ten thousand rupees" in sections 13(2) and 20A(3) of the principal enactment [Act 21/2026 §3][Act 21/2026 §4].
- The changes do not apply to offences committed before the Act came into operation [Act 21/2026 §5].

Caveats: The evidence summarises section 7's amendment only at bill level; the earlier Gazette text (044/2026, 2026-06-25) is a proposal, superseded by the Act.

question: Which 2025 bill proposes to revoke the 2024 legislation that introduced internet safety and content regulation measures?
answer:
The **Online Safety (Repeal)** bill — Bill 578/2025 (Gazette text, 8 April 2025) and Bill 590/2025 (presented 8 May 2025) — seeks to repeal the Online Safety Act, No. 9 of 2024, the law that governed internet platforms and online content.

- It states simply: "The Online Safety Act, No. 9 of 2024 is hereby repealed." [578/2025 §2; identical in 590/2025]
- It also repeals any regulations made under that Act after its enactment, from the date this repeal Act is enacted. [590/2025 §3]
- Short title: "Online Safety (Repeal) Act, No. of 2025". [590/2025 §1]

Caveats: This is a bill, not law — no certified Act is held for it (Acts checked up to 30 October 2026), so it has not been shown to have passed. The 2024 Act's own text is not in the evidence.

question: What 2025 legislation addresses re‑conducting postponed local council elections by allowing new nominations and setting a fresh election date?
answer:
The Local Authorities Elections (Special Provisions) Act, No. 1 of 2025 (certified 2025-02-17), which came from bills 565/2025 and 566/2025 [Act 1/2025].

- Nomination papers for the postponed 9 March 2023 elections to the scheduled authorities are "deemed to be of no force and effect as if such nomination papers had never been submitted", and the earlier notices are revoked, so fresh nominations are called [Act 1/2025 §2].
- The fresh nomination-notice date is not fixed in the Act: it is "such date as the Election Commission may determine by Order published in the Gazette", and must be "not later than three months from the date of coming into operation of this Act" [Act 1/2025 §3].

Caveats: The Act sets the date for nomination notices, not the poll date, and it applies only to the local authorities in its Schedule [Act 1/2025 §3].

question: Which 2025 bill updates the 2008 act that governs major strategic development projects in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Strategic Development Projects (Amendment) Act, No. 26 of 2025** (certified 2025-12-17) amends the Strategic Development Projects Act, No. 14 of 2008 [Act 26/2025 §2]. It originated as bill 643/2025 (Gazette text, 2025-11-07) and bill 650/2025 (Bill, 2025-11-14) [Act 26/2025; 650/2025; 643/2025].

- It substitutes "ten years" for "twenty-five years" in the proviso to section 2 of the 2008 Act, which was last amended by Act No. 12 of 2011 [Act 26/2025 §2].
- It replaces section 3 of the principal enactment, requiring BOI identification, Ministry of Finance ex-ante cost-benefit analysis "within one month", and a Gazette Order by the Minister with Cabinet concurrence [Act 26/2025 §3].
- It adds ex-post monitoring and enforcement, including suspension or revocation of exemptions and "administrative penalties" after a one-month show-cause notice [Act 26/2025 §4].

Caveats: This is an amending Act, not the consolidated text of the 2008 Act; the amended Act's full current wording is not in the evidence.

question: Which 2026 bill was introduced to legally establish the UnV charitable foundation?
answer:
Bill 010/2026, the **UnV Foundation (Incorporation)** bill presented on 2026-01-22 (an identical earlier Gazette text is 003/2026, 2026-01-09) — its long title is "An Act to incorporate the UnV Foundation" [010/2026 §1].

Caveats: This is a bill, not law; no certified Act is held (Acts checked to 2026-10-30), so it has not been shown to have passed [010/2026 §1].

question: Which 2025 bill updates Sri Lanka's 1979 criminal procedure legislation?
answer:
The Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act, No. 7 of 2025 — enacted from bill 579/2025 (dated 2025-04-08) and certified on 2025-06-20 — amends the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, No. 15 of 1979 [Act 7/2025 §1] [579/2025].

- Its long title states: "TO AMEND THE CODE OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE ACT, NO. 15 OF 1979" [Act 7/2025].
- The Act inserts new sections 144A and 144B on dispensing with a suspect's or accused's personal court attendance [Act 7/2025 §2].
- It also inserts sections 273A–273U and new Forms 24 and 25 in the Second Schedule [Act 7/2025 §5] [Act 7/2025 §6].

Caveats: The evidence is the amending Act, not the consolidated 1979 Code; the header also links it to bill 576/2025, whose separate text is not given.

question: What 2026 bill proposes the twenty‑second revision of Sri Lanka’s constitution?
answer:
Bill 065/2026, the **Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution**, presented on 2026-08-18 (with a Gazette text, Bill 057/2026, dated 2026-08-07). It is a bill only: no certified Act is held for it, so it has not been shown to have passed [065/2026].

- It replaces Article 107(5), setting Supreme Court retirement at 67 and Court of Appeal at 65, and requires the Chief Justice to retire at 67 or after six years in office, "whichever occurs earlier" [065/2026 §2].
- It amends Article 137, substituting "not more than twenty four other Judges" for "not more than nineteen" [065/2026 §3].

Caveats: Only the outline and these clauses are in evidence; the auto-generated summaries are hints, not clause text.

question: Which 2026 bill seeks to repeal the 1972 Tenancy Act (No. 7) in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Bill 006/2026, the **Rent (Repeal)** Bill (dated 2026-01-20), is the 2026 proposal: clause 2 states "The Rent Act, No. 7 of 1972 is hereby repealed" [006/2026 §2]. The Act it targets is the *Rent* Act, No. 7 of 1972 — not a "Tenancy Act" [006/2026 §2].

- It is a bill only: no certified Act is held for it (Acts checked to 2026-10-30), so it has not been shown to have passed [006/2026 §2].
- It carries one-year transitional limits: no ejectment suits and no rent above the "authorised rent" for one year from the relevant date [006/2026 §3].
- Earlier, near-identical texts exist: 526/2024 (Gazette text, 2024-07-19) and 555/2024 [526/2024 §3].

Caveats: the question's "Tenancy Act" name does not match the cited Rent Act, No. 7 of 1972.
